name: ARMORY-01
text: The 0 square at A4–B5 cannot touch any loop segments — cross out 4 edges.

name: ARMORY-02
text: The 3 square at D2–E3 needs every remaining open side to reach 3 — draw D2–E2, E2–E3, and D3–E3.

name: ARMORY-03
text: Because corner E1 of the 1 square at D1–E2 has no exits outside the square, using either corner side would force both (two sides on a 1) — so cross out D1–E1 and E1–E2.

name: ARMORY-04
text: Two orthogonally adjacent 3 squares (A3–B4 and B3–C4) must share their middle edge and use both opposite far sides without branching at their shared corners — draw B3–B4, A3–A4, and C3–C4; cross out B2–B3 and B4–B5.

name: ARMORY-04
text: The diagonal 3 squares at B3–C4 and C4–D5 cannot both turn sharply around their shared corner C4, so each must use both of its outer sides — draw B3–C3, D4–D5, and C5–D5.

name: ARMORY-05
text: A segment enters corner E2 of the 2 square at D1–E2, so at most one of its two open sides at E2 can be used — since the 2 square still needs 2 of its 3 remaining open sides, its other open side must be drawn and the other exit at E2 is blocked: draw D1–E1.

name: ARMORY-06
text: The Mid-loop dot sits directly on D1–E1, so draw D1–E1.

name: ARMORY-07
text: The Mid-loop dot at B1 cannot go straight vertically, so the loop must go straight horizontally through B1.

name: ARMORY-08
text: Because F3 must sit at the midpoint of its straight segment, extending the matching side forces draw F4–F5.

name: ARMORY-09
text: One end of the Mid-loop segment E2–F2 must turn immediately, so the opposite end must also turn immediately: cross out D2–E2.

name: ARMORY-10
text: The 0← clue at E6 allows zero parallel loop segments left from it — cross out A6–B6.

name: ARMORY-11
text: The 2← clue at D3 needs every remaining open segment left from it to reach 2 — draw B3–C3 and A3–B3.

name: ARMORY-12
text: The white wall at B2 must lie inside the loop while the board edge is outside, so the loop must pass between them — draw 6 segments.

name: ARMORY-13
text: The gray circle at A8 is in a corner and cannot go straight through, so it cannot be white — it must be a black circle.

name: ARMORY-14
text: The white circle at C1 cannot go vertically, so the loop must go straight horizontally through it.

name: ARMORY-15
text: The black circle at A3 leaves up, so it must go straight two cells up and cannot exit down.

name: ARMORY-16
text: The black circle at B3 is too close to the left edge to go two straight cells left, so it must go two cells right.

name: ARMORY-17
text: The gray circle at H6 cannot be black because it lacks room for two straight segments horizontally — it must be a white circle.

name: ARMORY-18
text: The touching black circles at D3 and D4 cannot connect (each must go straight through its neighbor), so D3 goes two cells up.

name: ARMORY-19
text: The white circle at C2 goes straight through D2, so the loop must turn at B2 (cross out A2–B2).

name: ARMORY-20
text: A5 has only one available exit left, so the loop cannot pass through it (cross out A5–B5).

name: ARMORY-15
text: A1 is on the loop and has only two exits left, so it must use A1–B1.

name: ARMORY-21
text: The black circle at C3 cannot enter B3 (which already has a perpendicular segment), so it must go two cells right.

name: ARMORY-22
text: D5 and D6 are the two ends of the same open path while other loop cells lie outside it, so D5–D6 cannot connect them.

name: ARMORY-20
text: Three white circles in a row (D2, C2, and B2) cannot go along the row because the middle circle would fail to turn at either end; all three must cross vertically.

name: ARMORY-23
text: Because corner C5 of the 2 square at B4–C5 has no outside exits, the two sides at that corner are either both on or both off — forcing draw C3–C4.

name: ARMORY-24
text: Because the loop passes straight through the white circle at D2, it uses exactly one of the 3 square's two sides at D2 — so both opposite sides of the 3 square must be drawn: draw C1–D1 and C1–C2.

name: ARMORY-23
text: The segment at F8 must continue along one of the 1 square's two adjacent sides at E7–F8, using up its single segment — so its two opposite sides are off: cross out E7–F7 and E7–E8.

name: ARMORY-25
text: Corner D4 must be visited and has only one open exit outside the 2 square at C3–D4, while the square can take at most one more segment — so D4 must use its outside exit and one side of the square, leaving no segments for the square's other open sides: cross out C3–D3.

name: ARMORY-26
text: A diagonal chain of 2s between the 3 squares at F5–G6 and D7–E8 prevents either 3 from using both sides facing the chain, forcing both outer corners — draw 4 segments.

name: ARMORY-27
text: Eliminating blocked stop lengths around the Mid-loop dot at E7–F7 forces cross out D7–E7 and F7–G7.

name: ARMORY-28
text: The Mid-loop dot at F6 has no valid symmetric straight length vertically, so it must run horizontally: draw E6–F6 and F6–G6; cross out F5–F6 and F6–F7.

name: ARMORY-29
text: Both 3← at J4 and 3← at G4 count the same total left, so there can be zero segments in the gap between them — cross out H4–I4.

name: ARMORY-30
text: Along the 3↓ ray from E2, turn limits along the ray leave zero spare capacity to reach 3 remaining segments — draw E3–E4 and E6–E7.

name: ARMORY-31
text: If the white circle at E4 went vertically, both ends would go straight without turning; so it must go straight horizontally.

name: ARMORY-22
text: E3 has only two exits left, and both lead to the ends of one path (E4 and D3): using it would close the loop early, so cross out E3–E4 and D3–E3.

name: ARMORY-32
text: G7 is on the loop with three exits, and two of them (H7 and G8) lead to the ends of one path; using both would close the loop early, so it must take G6–G7.

name: ARMORY-33
text: The touching white circles at E4 and F4 cannot join because C4–D4 already continues straight past E4; both must go vertically.

name: ARMORY-34
text: If the gray circle at F4 were white, it could not make a required 90° turn on either axis; so it must be a black circle.

name: ARMORY-35
text: The white circle at F3 must turn at one of its two ends, so it cannot go vertically (F2 is a white circle and F4 has both turns blocked); it must go horizontally.

name: ARMORY-36
text: C3 and C1 are the two ends of one open path while other loop cells lie outside it, so the black circle at C3 cannot extend two cells up into C1; it must go two cells down.

name: ARMORY-37
text: The black circle at F3 cannot send a ray right between the two diagonal white circles at G4 and G2 (doing so would block whichever side its second leg takes); so it must go two cells left.

name: ARMORY-38
text: The black circle at G3 cannot extend into the white circle at G5 because G6 already continues straight, leaving G5 unable to turn on either side; so G3 must go two cells up.

name: ARMORY-32
text: Because H4 must be visited and is already blocked on one perpendicular side, crossing out H3–H4 would also block the black circle at H5 from entering through H4–H5 — stranding H4. So draw H3–H4.

name: ARMORY-39
text: G6 has only two exits left, pointing to F6 and G5, which both already have a segment; passing through G6 would fill both neighbors and cut off the white circle at F5 on both axes, so cross out F6–G6 and G5–G6.

name: ARMORY-40
text: Drawing B2–C2 would fill both C2 and B2, turning B3 into a dead end and cutting off the white circle at C3 on both axes; so cross out B2–C2.

name: ARMORY-41
text: Inside/outside shading puts Outside on both sides of J4–J5, so the loop cannot pass between them (cross out J4–J5).

name: ARMORY-42
text: Checkerboard parity on the highlighted full-board region: light dots need 2 more segment ends and dark dots need 4 (difference 2), which forces draw D4–D5 and B6–C6; cross out B5–C5 and D6–D7.

name: ARMORY-43
text: Drawing C10–D10 would fill both C10 and D10, sealing both escapes of the adjacent pair C9–D9 and stranding the open end at C9; so cross out C10–D10.

name: ARMORY-44
text: The forced corridor (G1 and F1) only connects the two ends of one open path (G2 and F2) while other loop cells lie outside it: entering it would close the loop early, so cross out G1–G2, F1–G1, and F1–F2.

name: ARMORY-45
text: Checkerboard parity on the highlighted full-board region: light dots need 8 more segment ends and dark dots need 7 (difference 1), which forces draw A4–A5; cross out B4–B5.

name: ARMORY-41
text: Circle shading: crossing line B1–C1 makes B1–C2 Inside; flipping diagonally across white circle B2 makes A2–B3 Outside. That puts Outside on both sides of A2–A3, so cross out A2–A3.

name: ARMORY-46
text: Inside/outside shading: crossing line A1–B1 makes A1–B2 Inside; the 3 square A1–B2 makes B1–C2 Outside. That puts Outside on both sides of B1–C1, so cross out B1–C1.

name: ARMORY-47
text: The highlighted area has only two open ends (D1 and D2), so they must connect inside it; that makes B1 and B2 ends of one path, so B1–B2 cannot close them early.

name: ARMORY-48
text: Without E1–F1, B3 would be the only cell connecting the highlighted area to the rest of the loop (a single loop cannot pass through it twice), so E1–F1 must be drawn.

name: ARMORY-48
text: If you tried drawing C3–C4, the highlighted area would be sealed off with 3 open ends (odd, so they can't all pair up); therefore cross out C3–C4.

name: ARMORY-41
text: Without G3–H3, J5 would be the only cell connecting the highlighted area to the rest of the loop (a single loop cannot pass through it twice), so G3–H3 must be drawn.

name: ARMORY-49
text: If you tried drawing E3–E4, the highlighted area would be sealed off with 5 open ends (odd, so they can't all pair up); therefore cross out E3–E4.

name: ARMORY-50
text: Because this puzzle has top-bottom mirror symmetry and a unique solution, the single loop must cross the mirror axis exactly twice (2 crossings already known), so cross out 4 edges.

name: ARMORY-51
text: Imagine a segment at C6–C7 and follow the forced deductions (starting with: the white circle at C7 must go vertically; then the 2↓ clue at C2 already has 2 segments, so the rest of its ray is off; then C3 becomes a dead end; then B3 must use B3–B4; reaching a contradiction after 18 steps). So cross out C6–C7.

name: ARMORY-52
text: Imagine a segment at C2–D2: then the Mid-loop dot at C2 must extend symmetrically horizontally; and finally the Mid-loop dot at B3 has no valid symmetric straight segment. So cross out C2–D2.

name: ARMORY-53
text: Imagine a segment at G8–G9: then the black circle at H8 is blocked left and goes two cells right; then I9 becomes a dead end; then H9 becomes a dead end; and finally G9 is left with only one way out. So cross out G8–G9.

name: ARMORY-54
text: Imagine no segment at A5–B5: then A5 becomes a dead end; then the 1↓ clue at A3 needs all of its remaining open segments; then A6 must use A6–B6; then A7 must use A7–B7; then B6–B7 cannot close the loop early; then B7 must use B7–C7; then the 2↓ clue at C3 needs all of its remaining open segments; and finally the Castle Wall clue at F5 cannot reach 2 segments along its ray. So draw A5–B5.
